question: When an existing empty SQLite registry has a legacy runs.json source but no durable receipt, should doctor preserve and warn, automatically import, or require an explicit recovery action?
rationale: No stored provenance can distinguish an authoritative never-imported source from stale data previously imported and later deleted, so either automatic choice can hide runs or resurrect intentionally removed state.

options.title: Preserve and offer recovery
options.body: Keep the source untouched, warn clearly, and provide an explicit doctor recovery action that lets the operator import or discard it.

options.title: Import whenever SQLite is empty
options.body: Preserve historical automatic recovery behavior but accept that stale legacy runs can be resurrected when provenance is absent.

options.title: Pause this migration change
options.body: Keep the PR open until a broader legacy-state recovery contract is designed and proven across other SQLite migrations.

recommendation.title: Preserve and offer recovery
recommendation.body: Keep the source untouched, warn clearly, and provide an explicit doctor recovery action that lets the operator import or discard it.

likelyOwner.reason: The behavior originates in the SQLite registry implementation they introduced, making them the strongest available owner for its upgrade contract.
